countedBy: lane #201 (opus) from the frontal Commons photograph by Chabe01 (2024-11-25, CC BY-SA 4.0, staging/landmarks/effectenbeurs/commons/c05.jpg) before the model was rendered; not a blind haiku count, the integrator may re-count. One window is one opening; the attic lights stand between stone piers about 0.35-0.4 m wide, so each light is counted; the barred ground windows are counted per pane pair member; the frontispiece portals are glazed. Dormers are roof and are cropped off with heightM.

facades.name: Beursplein, north-east pavilion (right of its door axis)
facades.note: c05 x 95-410: ground: door-like opening, the shop window, a narrow window; first floor: two windows and a narrow one; second floor: the five-light group and a narrow window; attic: the five lights and the right pair. The left door axis (door, two small windows stacked over it, narrow window, attic pair) is cropped off.

facades.name: Beursplein, left wing
facades.note: c05 x 410-695: three axes; pairs of small barred windows in the granite; three cross windows on each brick floor; a group of three lights per axis in the attic. No 'columns' count: the attic three-light groups (1.0 m pitch), the ground pane pairs (1.1 m pitch, centred on the axis; in c05 they appear shifted outward because the granite plinth projects in front of the brick) and the cross windows interleave within 0.5 m, so the clustered-axis measure cannot separate them; the earlier declared 9 was the attic light count, already checked by the attic row.

facades.name: Beursplein, frontispiece
facades.note: c05 x 750-1035 between the big banded pilasters: three portals, three windows under the balcony (partly behind the lamp and the tree; Commons Kleon3 2025 shows all three), three balcony doors, nine attic lights in three groups. Pediment above the crop.

facades.name: Beursplein, right wing
facades.note: c05 x 1090-1380, the same order as the left wing. No 'columns' count: the attic three-light groups (1.0 m pitch), the ground pane pairs (1.1 m pitch, centred on the axis; in c05 they appear shifted outward because the granite plinth projects in front of the brick) and the cross windows interleave within 0.5 m, so the clustered-axis measure cannot separate them; the earlier declared 9 was the attic light count, already checked by the attic row.

facades.name: Beursplein, south-west pavilion
facades.note: c05 x 1545-1870: three axes, one window per axis on the ground and brick floors, a pair of lights per axis in the attic; the wide corner pilaster with Mercury's niche on the right makes it asymmetric.

calibration: alongM crops calibrated 2026-11-02 by mirror-symmetry sweep of the model elevation (wings and frontispiece) and by matching the photo's openings per row (pavilions); the photo counts were written before the model existed and were not changed.
